I've been farming this land for 30 years, and I know what works around here. My 6 mu in Quzhou County — I split it the same way every year: all 6 mu for winter wheat in the cool season, then I turn it right around into summer maize after the wheat comes off in early June. It's the only way to get two crops in one year on this plain, and I've got the well to water them when the rains don't cooperate.

For the wheat, I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station — it's not the fanciest hybrid, but it yields steady and I can save some seed if I need to. I'll rotary till before planting in mid-October. Fertilizer? I'll put down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 6 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium at the base. I'll irrigate four times: once after sowing to get it germinated, once before winter to protect the seedlings from freezing, once at jointing in spring when the wheat really needs a push, and once at grain filling. I'll spray pesticides twice — once in early spring for aphids and diseases, and once before heading. I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather holds.

As soon as the wheat is harvested in early June, I'll rotary till again and plant summer maize with a hybrid seed — the county extension office recommends hybrids for summer maize, and I agree, they give better yield in the short summer window. Maize needs heat, and we've got that, but it also needs water at the right times. I'll irrigate three times: at sowing, at the big trumpet stage, and at grain filling. Fertilizer will be 16 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium. I'll spray pesticides twice — once when the armyworms show up, and once for corn borers. With a good summer, I can get 550 kg per mu from the maize.

My wife and I can't do everything alone anymore — my son works in the city — so I hire a combine for harvest and a tractor for tillage. The off-farm income helps pay for the fertilizer and seed, but I still do the irrigating and spraying myself because I know every corner of these 6 mu.
